model.partySelection: Three fixed six-species ordinary coverage parties, selected before opponent sampling. No box counter-drafting. The same six species face every opponent. Level assignment rotates over six party slots independently of opponent variant. Lead is chosen only from those six after seeing enemy lead. The enemy lineup is always getTimberLeagueNextTeam; player order/levels cannot change enemy species.
model.typePolicy: Choose affordable damaging moves by type effectiveness × STAB, then listed power; no damage/speed prediction. Switch when the current member is type-disadvantaged and another is materially better, at least two actions apart except exhausted MP. Heal active member at HP<=35%, MP<=10, or disruptive status. Lead and forced replacement use type matchup × squared visible level ratio; no damage prediction, and levels are never reassigned to counter the enemy.
model.damagePolicy: Choose expected-damage moves using current stats, HP, MP, type, accuracy and speed. Compare current matchup, switching entry damage and healing. No enemy action/RNG lookahead. Switch at least two actions apart unless no damaging move. Forced replacement and lead use predicted matchup.
model.battleRuntime: Production executeBattleMove plus production turn-start/end, speed/priority, move message/order helpers, AI and its exact trainerStyle. Production transition helper counts every player move attempt, potion or voluntary switch once. Forced replacements are free. Enemy voluntary switch count comes from the shared helper and recall logs. Enemy send-outs, status logs and switch intention messages are retained for AI cooldown. Enemy switches preserve temporary state, matching production. Player switches clear temporary state.
model.items: Only max_potion (超级伤药), capped at 0 or 2 per simulated challenge; active-only recovery, no revival. This simulation cap is not a new game rule. Opponents have zero potions.
model.residuals: Match current production asymmetry: regular move turns tick residual statuses on surviving active members; potion/switch reply turns do so only when a member faints. This may merit a separate gameplay decision but was not changed for calibration.
limits: Headless deterministic decision policies, not human win rates or optimal play.
All teams start full HP/MP with default level moves and no permanent boosts, battle items, custom TM plans or Dynamax.
No strategy plans multi-turn setup/status combinations; a no_usable_damage_policy stop may still be legally playable via status moves or residual damage.
Advanced policy knows current opposing stats/moves as previous tactical audit did; type policy deliberately does not predict damage.
No animation, UI, cloud persistence, disconnect/retry or resource synchronization simulation.
No battle-time experience/level growth; league currently settles rewards on final victory.

The 100/30/30/30/30/30 profile is a structural stress test: some final evolutions cannot naturally exist at Lv.30. It is not used for ordinary-player calibration. The legal-one-high extra run uses 100/60/60/60/60/60.
Wilson intervals describe seeded random-battle uncertainty conditional on these fixed policies and parties, not player population uncertainty.
